context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data isolation to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Clinicians (Client Applications)
* Global Traffic Director / API Gateway
* Regional Stacks (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US)
* AI Symptom Checker Service
* Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem
* External Identity and Consent Provider
* National E-Prescription Gateways and Pharmacy Networks
* External Notification and Messaging Service
* External Payment Gateways and Billing Systems

## Relationships
* Client Applications interact with the Global Traffic Director via HTTPS and WebSockets.
* Global Traffic Director routes regional traffic to `europe-west3` or `us-central1` via mTLS.
* Regional Stacks communicate with National E-Prescription Gateways using HL7 FHIR (US) and national standards (EU).
* Regional Stacks integrate with External Identity and Consent Providers using OpenID Connect (OIDC).
* Regional Stacks process payments via External Payment Gateways using REST APIs over HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
* Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Selected for regional availability in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
* HL7 FHIR: Enforces interoperability standards for US healthcare data exchange.
* WebSockets and Adaptive Bitrate Streaming: Ensures video consultations operate in degraded modes below 300 kbit/s.
* mTLS: Secures all internal inter-service and cross-boundary communications.

## Rationale
Isolating infrastructure into GCP `europe-west3` and `us-central1` guarantees that EU and US health data remain strictly within their respective jurisdictions to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA. Decoupled regional boundaries and explicit API gateways maintain high availability, traceability, and low-bandwidth resilience.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and the US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for rural users via isolated regional deployments on GCP.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (Primary Users)
- Global Traffic Director / API Gateway
- Regional Deployment Units (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US)
- API Gateway / Ingress Controller Containers
- Consent Enforcement Middleware/Proxy Containers
- Stateless Core Application Containers
- Video Streaming Gateway Containers with Local Storage/Caching Agents
- AI Inference & Audit Proxy Containers
- FHIR Translation Adapter Container (US) and National E-Prescription Adapter Container (EU)
- Local Async Event Bus / Queue Containers
- Configuration and Secrets Management Sidecars
- Observability & Telemetry Exporter Sidecars with PII/PHI Stripping

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians connect to Regional API Gateways via HTTPS and WebRTC (TURN/STUN).
- Core Application Containers route traffic through Consent Enforcement Middleware via gRPC/REST.
- Video Streaming Gateway utilizes adaptive bitrate streaming over WebRTC for unstable connections (<300 kbit/s).
- US Core connects to external pharmacies via HL7 FHIR; EU Core connects via national e-prescription standards.
- AI Inference & Audit Proxy synchronously logs inputs, model versions, and outputs before returning urgency recommendations.
- Local Async Event Bus buffers telemetry locally during network drops and syncs to Regional Audit Subsystems upon reconnection.

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider:** Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` to enforce strict regional data residency.
- **Streaming Protocol:** WebRTC over TURN/STUN for resilient, low-bandwidth video consultations.
- **Interoperability Standards:** HL7 FHIR (US) and national e-prescription APIs (EU).
- **Messaging/Buffering:** Lightweight MQTT / local message broker for async event queuing during unstable rural connections.
- **Security & Networking:** mTLS for internal container communications and strict network isolation policies.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regulatory compliance (GDPR and HIPAA) by isolating data processing within regional GCP boundaries and enforcing explicit consent via dedicated middleware. Furthermore, the stateless container design coupled with adaptive streaming and local event buffering ensures high availability and traceability even for rural users with unstable internet connections.

API Gateway / Ingress Controller Contain.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, HIPAA, GDPR, and EU MDR compliance on Google Cloud Platform.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Clinicians (End Users)
- API Gateway / Ingress Controller Containers (Google Cloud Platform Ingress / Envoy)
- Stateless Core Application Containers (GCP Microservices)
- Video Streaming Gateway Containers (WebRTC, TURN/STUN)
- AI Inference & Audit Proxy Containers (Python / gRPC)
- FHIR Translation Adapter Container (US) and National E-Prescription Adapter Container (EU)
- Consent Enforcement Middleware/Proxy Containers

## Relationships
- Patients and Clinicians -> API Gateway / Ingress Controller Containers: Connect via HTTPS and WebRTC (TURN/STUN)
- Global Traffic Director / API Gateway -> API Gateway / Ingress Controller Containers: Routes regional traffic via mTLS
- API Gateway / Ingress Controller Containers -> Stateless Core Application Containers: Forwards validated requests via internal gRPC/HTTP
- API Gateway / Ingress Controller Containers -> AI Inference & Audit Proxy Containers: Routes symptom checker payloads via gRPC

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions ensuring data residency.
- Envoy Proxy / GCP Ingress: Manages ingress routing, token-bucket rate limiting, TLS termination, and schema validation.
- WebRTC and TURN/STUN: Powers real-time video consultations supporting degraded rural connections.
- OpenTelemetry: Captures distributed tracing headers (W3C Trace Context) and telemetry with PII/PHI stripping.
- RFC 7807 Problem Details: Standardizes error response schemas across all gateway error paths.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict regional data residency by isolating EU and US workloads while ensuring high availability for rural users via optimized gateways. Envoy-based rate limiting, schema validation, and rigorous security hardening protect core microservices and maintain compliance with healthcare standards.

Consent Enforcement Middleware/Proxy Con.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients on GCP. It enforces strict regional data residency, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and auditability.

## Key Elements
* Consent Enforcement Middleware/Proxy Containers: Custom Middleware / Envoy Proxy
* Local Edge Cache: Redis
* External Systems: External Identity and Consent Provider, Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem
* Downstream Services: Stateless Core Application Containers, Video Streaming Gateway Containers, AI Inference & Audit Proxy Containers

## Relationships
* Client to Consent Middleware: Route requests with JWT tokens [HTTPS / gRPC]
* Consent Middleware to Redis Cache: Perform fast local lookups and cache-aside operations [Redis Protocol]
* Consent Middleware to External Identity Provider: Fallback validation and token retrieval [HTTPS / REST]
* Consent Middleware to Core Containers: Forward requests with enriched metadata headers (`X-Consent-Purpose`, `X-Data-Residency-Region`) [gRPC / HTTP]
* Consent Middleware to Telemetry Subsystem: Emit asynchronous structured audit logs [OpenTelemetry / gRPC]

## Technology Stack
* Envoy Proxy: Provides the ExtAuthz filter and ingress traffic routing
* Redis: Used for local edge caching of consent tokens to reduce latency
* GCP (europe-west3, us-central1): Cloud provider and target regions ensuring data residency compliance
* W3C Trace Context: Used for distributed tracing propagation (`traceparent` headers)

## Rationale
This architecture uses local caching and the ExtAuthz filter to enforce strict default-deny privacy controls without introducing latency bottlenecks during video consultations. Decoupling consent logic via proxies ensures regional data residency and GDPR/HIPAA compliance across cross-border boundaries.

Stateless Core Application Containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency on Google Cloud Platform while ensuring high availability for unstable rural connections.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Clinicians (Users)
* Stateless Core Application Containers (Containerized Microservices on GCP)
* Consent Enforcement Middleware/Proxy Containers (Custom Middleware / Envoy Proxy)
* External Identity and Consent Provider (OIDC)
* Regional Adapters (FHIR Translation Adapter for US, National E-Prescription Adapter for EU)
* AI Inference & Audit Proxy Containers (Python / gRPC)
* Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem

## Relationships
* Stateless Core Application Containers -> Consent Enforcement Middleware/Proxy Containers: Route traffic via gRPC/REST
* Stateless Core Application Containers -> External Identity and Consent Provider: Authenticate and verify consent using OpenID Connect (OIDC)
* Stateless Core Application Containers -> Regional Adapters: Transmit health data using HL7 FHIR (US) or National APIs (EU)
* Stateless Core Application Containers -> Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem: Log inputs, model versions, and consent tokens via OpenTelemetry

## Technology Stack
* Google Cloud Platform (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Core hosting environment ensuring data residency compliance.
* Envoy Proxy / Custom Middleware: Enforces zero-trust mTLS, fail-closed security, and consent checks.
* OpenTelemetry: Powers distributed tracing, telemetry export, and strict PII/PHI log redaction.
* OpenAPI / JSON Schema: Enforces payload sanitization, size limiting, and RFC 7807 problem details.

## Rationale
Strict region-bound container deployments and fail-closed security ensure uncompromised GDPR and HIPAA compliance without cross-border data leakage. Idempotent APIs, circuit breakers, and graceful shutdowns (`SIGTERM`) maintain resilient, degraded-mode availability for rural patients on unstable connections.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker across the EU and US. It ensures stringent GDPR and HIPAA compliance while supporting unstable rural internet connections.

## Key Elements
* Configuration and Secrets Management Sidecars (GCP Secret Manager Sidecar)
* Stateless Core Application Containers
* GCP Cloud KMS (Key Management Service)
* Local Loopback Unix Domain Socket
* Observability & Telemetry Exporter Sidecars (Prometheus / OpenTelemetry)

## Relationships
* Sidecars communicate with GCP Secret Manager via gRPC/HTTPS for configuration and secrets retrieval
* Sidecars deliver configuration to Core Application Containers via local loopback Unix domain sockets
* Sidecars communicate with GCP Cloud KMS via secure APIs for ciphertext encryption and decryption
* Sidecars emit Prometheus metrics to Observability Exporter Sidecars for sync status tracking

## Technology Stack
* GCP Secret Manager Sidecar: Manages credentials and configuration decoupling from application code
* GCP Cloud KMS: Provides keys for ciphertext encryption at rest for locally cached files
* Local Unix Domain Socket: Transmits configurations securely without plain-text environment variables
* Prometheus / OpenTelemetry: Emits and exports sidecar sync status, cache rates, and decryption health metrics

## Rationale
This architecture uses GCP Secret Manager sidecars with local caching and circuit-breakers to ensure high availability and resilient bootstrapping during unstable rural network conditions. Strict IAM scoping, Unix domain sockets, and KMS encryption at rest maintain rigorous HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

## Overview
• The system is a Cross-Border Telehealth Platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US.
• It ensures strict data residency, privacy, and traceability compliance via regional GCP deployments and secure telemetry pipelines.

• Telemetry sidecars export sanitized logs and metrics to regional OpenTelemetry backends in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.

• Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider ensuring isolated regional processing in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
• OpenTelemetry (OTel) Collector framework: Used for telemetry collection, PII/PHI stripping, and local file buffering.
• WebRTC and TURN/STUN: Protocols powering real-time video consultations under unstable connections.
• HL7 FHIR and National E-Prescription APIs: Interoperability standards for US and EU prescription routing.

## Rationale
• Regional GCP isolation and strict telemetry stripping enforce GDPR and HIPAA compliance while keeping health data local.
• Local buffering and fail-closed sanitization protect application availability and security during unstable rural network conditions.
